title: VegasInsider Picks Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: VegasInsider Premium review, checked 20 Nov 2026: plan prices, the no refund policy, what the self graded expert records show, and what users report.
dek: A long running odds site, founded in 1997 and owned by Better Collective since 2019, that sells one subscription to every pick from its roster of experts for $19.99 a month or $119.99 a year. VegasInsider grades its own experts and shows leaderboards, but we could not open a full pick log without paying, and the subscription has no refunds.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for any VegasInsider expert. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: VegasInsider is a real, well known betting media site. Its terms name Better Collective USA, Inc. as the operator, its prices are posted, and its experts are named people with long public careers. In that sense the Premium subscription is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question. VegasInsider grades its own experts at $100 per pick and posts leaderboards. On 20 Nov 2026 Mark Franco was 611-485 (56%) and +$6,465 this year, and Stephen Nover was 754-677 (53%) and +$3,507. Those are full counts, which is better than most sellers offer, but they are graded by the seller, only the top four names show, and the pick by pick log was not open to us without a subscription. VegasInsider's own guide to handicappers tells bettors to look for records from independent platforms and audited results, which its own boards are not.

Treat VegasInsider Premium as a cheap bundle of opinions from a seller that earns most of its money from sportsbook signups. If you try it, start with the $4.99 pass, cancel before it rolls into $19.99 a month if you do not want it, record every pick with the line and the time you saw it, and remember the plans are not refundable.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. The refund policy says "There is a no refund policy on Vegas Insider Premium monthly or annual subscriptions" and "refunds will not be provided due to poor predictive performance." The only refunds it describes are for unauthorized or fraudulent card charges, reviewed case by case. It does end by saying that customers who feel entitled to a refund for whatever reason can reach out and the company will work with them.

Plans renew on their own. The Why Buy page says "all subscriptions will be automatically billed at the end of your product, either monthly or annually," and the 3 Day Pass says it continues at $19.99 per month. A buyer who only wants a short trial needs to cancel before the pass ends. The Delivery Policy says access starts at once from the Expert Picks or My Products page after signing in. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: How we checked: we read the all sports, current year leaderboard on 7 Nov 2026 and again on 20 Nov 2026, and worked out what changed in between. Profit is VegasInsider's own figure at $100 per pick. Mark Franco's 611 wins and 485 losses would earn about $7,750 if every pick were a standard -110 bet; the board shows $6,465, which suggests his average price was worse than -110 or that some losses were at bigger prices. Either way he is profitable by the board's count, at roughly 5% to 6% of money risked.

Stephen Nover's 754-677 is 52.7%. At -110 a bettor needs 52.4% to break even, so the board's +$3,507 over 1,431 picks works out to about $2.45 per $100 pick. That is a thin edge that the price a buyer actually gets could erase.

VegasInsider does more than most pick sellers here. The Why Buy page says it grades every expert at one unit ($100) per pick, does not allow experts "to pad their records with multiple unit wagers," shows the pick, the publish time and the odds, and requires picks to post at least one hour before the game. Those are good rules. But the grading is done by the company that sells the picks, and the full logs were not open to us without paying.

The leaderboard shows only the top four names per board. A buyer sees the leaders, not the experts who are losing. Bet Labs sits on the percentage board with 96 picks and no change in 13 days. The profile highlights are titles picked from past seasons, and Stephen Nover's profile covers results only "heading into 2021". The free picks pages show records over the last 3 or 7 days, such as 3-0 in the last 7 days, which are too short to mean anything.
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for VegasInsider expert picks plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found none, so there is no Watchdog graded sample for this seller yet.

What is independently verifiable: very little. No third party grades the VegasInsider experts, and we found no regulator records for them. One profile claim points to an outside contest: Mark Franco's bio says he finished fifth in the 2003 Hilton SuperContest at 76-57. We could not find the contest's own standings online to check it.

What is the seller's own record keeping: the Expert Records leaderboards, graded by VegasInsider at $100 per pick. On 20 Nov 2026 the all sports current year board showed Prop Model 612-488 (56%, +$7,528), Mark Franco 611-485 (56%, +$6,465), Stephen Nover 754-677 (53%, +$3,507) and Bet Labs 62-34 (65%, +$2,446). These are full counts, not streaks, which is better than most sellers offer, but we could not open the pick by pick log behind them, so we could not check the prices, the post times or the experts left off the board.

Company background: VegasInsider says it has run since 1997. Better Collective, a sports betting affiliate company (Better Collective A/S), bought VegasInsider and ScoresandOdds in Jul 2019 for $20 million in cash, and said at the time it would move the sites from a subscription based tips model to an affiliate (referral) model. The site today carries promo code pages for dozens of sportsbooks, casinos, sweepstakes casinos and prediction markets beside the picks.
What is marketing: the short records shown next to free picks, the season titles on each profile, and the three testimonials on the Premium page.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no VegasInsider expert is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: VegasInsider says a handicapper needs to be right 55% of the time, and its leading experts this year sit between 53% and 56%. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on VegasInsider Premium is thin. The largest sample is the iPhone app rating, which covers the whole app, not just the picks. Forum bettors talk about VegasInsider mostly as an odds and data site. We found no Reddit thread or forum post from a paying Premium buyer describing the picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Across the App Store, two betting forums and a long running TheRX thread, users talk about VegasInsider as an odds, trends and consensus site far more than as a picks seller. The App Store rating is high (4.7 from 2.4K ratings), and the visible reviews from 2022 to 2026 split between longtime users who call it their go to source and users unhappy with a redesign, with consensus data moving behind a paywall, and with one touch in app sign ups that one reviewer said cost them $40. In 2022 Sportsbook Review and Covers members complained that a redesign made the odds pages harder to use and more crowded with ads, and one claimed, without evidence, that its betting percentage data had been shaped by sponsor sportsbooks. Older posts on TheRX from 2014 show members passing around a VegasInsider weekly tip sheet. We found no buyer describing results from the paid Premium picks, positive or negative, and BBB had no listing.
The VegasInsider Betting Tips iPhone app showed 4.7 out of 5 from 2.3K ratings. The rating covers odds, news and other app features, so it says little about whether the paid picks win.
An App Store reviewer said sign ups in the app happen with one touch and no confirmation, said this had cost them $40, and praised the content otherwise.

An App Store reviewer said the new version was much worse: trends could only be seen game by game, and once a game started the app showed nothing but closing lines, which made it useless to them for live betting.
Another App Store reviewer said the app used to be their go to source for consensus data and complained that consensus numbers now sit behind a paywall, though they accepted paying for picks.

Other App Store reviewers were positive about the app as an information source: one called it the only site that covers everything a bettor needs and noted it is based in Fort Lauderdale, others called it accurate and up to date or their go to site for years, and one said they use its spreads and trends in a confidence pool. None mentions the paid picks or whether they win.

Two App Store reviewers liked the tool but asked for changes: one wanted the betting and money percentages updated more often because they moved sharply before kickoff, and the other wanted the team numbers shown next to each team as before.

In a long running newsletters thread on TheRX, members shared and asked for issues of a VegasInsider weekly tip sheet alongside other paid newsletters. The posts pass the sheet around rather than judge its results, so they show reach, not performance.
The Premium page shows three testimonials from "VIP Subscribers" identified by first name and state. They are chosen by VegasInsider, so they cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.

BBB returned no results for VegasInsider. Trustpilot refused our request, and we found no Reddit thread in the main betting subreddits, and no TheRX, Covers or SBR discussion, about results from the paid Premium picks.

conflicts: VegasInsider earns from the betting companies it promotes. Its affiliate disclosure says "we may collect a share of sales or other compensation from the company links provided on this Website." Reports on the 2019 purchase by Better Collective, in Gambling Insider and SBC News, said the new owner would change the site's model from subscriptions and betting tips to affiliate marketing and lead generation.

The picks sit beside those offers. The NFL free picks page links to a BetMGM bonus code page, which on 20 Nov 2026 still promoted code VIBONUS. The site menus carry promo code pages for sportsbooks, prediction markets, casinos and sweepstakes casinos. Each page footer says the site contains commercial content and links the disclosure.
VegasInsider's own guide to the best handicappers lists its own experts first and tells readers to prefer independent, audited records. The guide is written by the same company that sells the picks.
The iPhone app lists RotoGrinders as developer and Rical LLC as seller, not VegasInsider.
strengths: A named corporate operator owned by Better Collective, with posted prices and published refund, delivery and terms pages.
Clear grading rules on paper: one unit ($100) per pick, no multi unit padding, picks posted at least an hour before the game, per the Why Buy page.
Leaderboards show full won and lost counts for the leaders, not just hot streaks, and the leaders were profitable by the board's count in 2026.
Low price for access to every expert: about 33 cents a day on the annual plan, with a $4.99 short pass to try it.
Named experts with long public careers, such as Mark Franco and Stephen Nover, rather than anonymous handles.
concerns: No refunds on monthly or annual plans, and plans renew automatically. The $4.99 pass rolls into $19.99 a month.
Records are graded by the seller. The pick by pick log was not open to us without paying, and the boards show only the top four names.
The leading experts' edges are thin: Stephen Nover's 53% is barely above break even at -110.
The site earns from sportsbook signups and promo codes placed next to its picks.
Prices differ between the Premium page, the Why Buy page and the iPhone app, and one App Store reviewer described accidental one touch sign ups.
No independent buyer account of the paid picks' results, positive or negative.
checklist: Start with the $4.99 3 Day Pass and set a reminder to cancel before it rolls into $19.99 a month.
Pick one or two experts and open their full pick history once you are inside. Count units at the prices you could actually get, not the leaderboard's figure.
Look past the top four on the leaderboard: ask how many experts on the roster lost money this year.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line and the time.
Ignore 3 day and 7 day records on the free picks pages. They are too short to mean anything.
Keep the picks and the sportsbook offers apart in your mind: the site is paid when you sign up with a book.
Give any expert a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes in the narrow sense: VegasInsider is a real media business operated by Better Collective USA, with posted prices and named experts. We could not verify that its experts win over time, because the records are graded by VegasInsider and the full logs were not open to us.
How much does VegasInsider Premium cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 the Premium page listed $19.99 a month, $119.99 a year, or a 3 Day Pass for $4.99 that then bills $19.99 per month. The refund policy says monthly and annual plans are not refundable, and plans renew automatically.
Do VegasInsider experts have a verified record?

Not independently. VegasInsider grades its own experts at $100 per pick and posts leaderboards, such as Mark Franco at 611-485 (56%) and Stephen Nover at 754-677 (53%) this year, but no third party checks them and we could not open the pick by pick log without paying.
Can I get a refund from VegasInsider?

The policy says no refunds on monthly or annual plans and none for poor predictive performance. It describes refunds only for unauthorized or fraudulent charges, though it says customers who feel entitled to one can contact the company.

Better Collective, a sports betting affiliate company, through Better Collective USA, Inc. It bought VegasInsider and ScoresandOdds in Jul 2019 for $20 million. The site also earns from sportsbook signups.

For the price you get every pick and write up from the whole roster, plus betting trends. What is unproven is whether following any expert makes money after the -110 juice, so a record you keep yourself is the only way to judge it, and the plan will not be refunded if the picks lose.
